transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... things have been really tense at my job lately. I'm a transportation inspector, and ever since I got this county safety award a while back, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports. 

They keep asking these really pointed budget questions, like... like they’re trying to make me look crooked or something. I brought it up to my supervisor, and he says it’s just a normal review process, but... I mean, I can tell what's going on. It's pretty obvious there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me. So, I guess I'm here to talk about how to deal with that.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear?

No, I've never had anything like that happen. I don't hear voices or anything. It's just... it's just the stuff happening at work with my reports and the budget questions. That's what's been bothering me.
Have you felt that people in other areas of your life—like your friends, family, or neighbors—are also acting in ways that suggest they have hidden, malicious motives toward you?

No, nothing like that. My friends and family are fine. It's... it's strictly a work thing. My neighbors just keep to themselves, so no issues there. I don't have any problems with anyone outside of the job. It's literally just those specific people at the county office messing with my reports. Everything else in my life is completely normal.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate or organize your thoughts since these issues at work began?

No, my concentration is fine. I mean, I can still do my job perfectly well, organize my thoughts, all of that. It's just... frustrating, you know? Having to double-check everything I submit because I know they're going to try and twist it. But my actual ability to focus hasn't changed at all.
Have you been feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or perhaps more energetic and impulsive than usual over the past few months?

No, I haven't really felt any of that. I'm not depressed or anything, and I definitely don't have these bursts of energy where I'm doing crazy things. I'm just a normal guy trying to do my job as an inspector. Like I said, the only thing really getting to me is the stress from work, dealing with what they're doing to my reports. But my mood overall is just... normal.
How long have you felt that these people at your office have been trying to discredit you?

It's been... about a year now. Yeah, right around a year. It started right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. Ever since then, it's just been this constant effort to make me look bad.
Have these concerns about your colleagues caused you to miss work, lose your job, or have any formal disciplinary actions taken against you?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been written up or suspended or anything. I mean... I still get to work on time every day, I complete all my inspections, keep up with church, and take care of myself just fine. 

The main problems really only come up when people bring up those reports, or... well, when they start questioning my spending. But as far as keeping my job and doing my day-to-day, no, it hasn't caused me to miss work or get in formal trouble.
Do you feel that you possess any special talents, insights, or connections that make you a target for this scrutiny at work?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't have any secret connections or... special talents or anything. I'm just a regular guy. 

I mean, I'm good at my job, and I got that safety recognition, but that was just from doing the work the way it's supposed to be done. I don't think I'm some kind of genius or anything like that. I just do things by the book, and I think that makes them look bad, so they mess with my reports to cover themselves. But no, there's nothing really special about me.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your supervisor's claim about this being a normal review process might actually be true?

I mean... I hear him when he says that. He tells me it's just standard procedure, just normal review. But... no, I don't really believe it. 

It's just too much of a coincidence, you know? Like I said, it all started right after that county safety award. Before that, everything was fine. Now, all of a sudden, they're twisting my inspection reports around, and asking me these really pointed questions about the budget. It's like they're trying to make me look crooked or something. 

So, yeah, my supervisor says it's normal, but... I can tell. I can just tell there's a coordinated effort going on to discredit me. It's not just a regular review.
Are there any other beliefs you hold that might seem unusual to other people, such as feeling that your physical health is being targeted or that you have some sort of secret mission?

No, definitely not. I don't think anyone is trying to poison me or mess with my health, nothing like that. And I don't have any kind of secret mission. Like I said, I'm just a normal guy trying to do my job the right way. It's just the stuff at work with the reports and the budget that's the problem. Everything else in my life is completely normal.

Do you feel that these colleagues at work have any specific, tangible evidence they are using to justify their actions, or is it strictly based on your interpretation of their behavior and the timing of these events?

No, they don't have any real evidence, because I haven't done anything wrong. That's the whole point. They're just... they're taking my normal reports and finding ways to twist them. 

Like, if I write up a safety violation, they'll say I'm being too aggressive or misinterpreting the code, and then they'll ask me all these questions about how much it's going to cost to fix it. It's not based on facts. It's just based on them wanting to make me look bad since I got that award. So, no, there's no actual evidence against me. It's just what I see them doing every day.
Do you believe that anyone outside of your immediate workplace, such as people in the community or government officials, is involved in or aware of this effort to discredit you?

No, no, I don't think it goes that far. It's really just the people at my office. I haven't noticed anyone in the community or... or any government officials acting weird or anything like that. It's just my supervisor and the other guys involved in the review process. They're the ones twisting my words and trying to make me look bad. Outside of work, everything is pretty much normal. No one else seems to know or care about it.
Do you feel that you have any special or unique abilities, or that you are meant for a higher purpose than your current job?

No, definitely not. I don't have any kind of special powers or anything. I'm just a regular guy. Like I said, I'm a transportation inspector. That's my job, and I'm good at it, but I don't think I'm meant for some grand higher purpose or anything like that. I just want to do my job without people messing with my reports. That's all.
Have you ever seen these colleagues communicate with each other in a way that you are certain is a coded signal intended to mock or threaten you?

No, I... I haven't seen anything like that. They aren't using secret codes or hand signals or anything weird. It's not like a spy movie or something. They just talk normally to each other, but it's what they actually do with my reports that's the problem. So, no, I haven't noticed any coded signals meant to threaten me. They just do what they're doing right out in the open when they review my work.
